events.text: At a marsh-side inn the tea arrives the colour of a bruise. Across the room the Poison Widow of Black Reed Marsh watches you over a lacquered fan. Ding. The Hunger has smelled something in the cup, and it is delighted.
events.arc: The Widow of Black Reed Marsh

choices.text: Drink it and let the Hunger eat the poison

effects.log: The poison goes down like cold fire and the Hunger eats every drop. The Widow's fan stops moving.

choices.text: Name the poison before you touch it

ok.log: "Seven-step moth, aged in a gourd," you say. The Widow laughs for the first time in years.

fail.log: You sniff too deep, guess wrong and spend the night coughing in the stable.

choices.text: Pour it into the reeds and leave

effects.log: By morning the reeds by the door are black. You are three villages away.

events.text: A green paper crane finds you on the road. Inside, in elegant script: the Widow has brewed the nine poisons of her life's work and wishes to learn which of them a stomach like yours cannot eat. She names a hilltop and promises an antidote, "probably".
events.arc: The Widow of Black Reed Marsh

choices.text: Go, and eat all nine

ok.log: Nine cups, nine colours, and the Hunger purrs through every one. The Widow sits down on the grass, very quietly.

fail.log: The seventh cup is one even the Hunger chokes on. You lie on the hill two days while the Widow takes notes.

choices.text: Go, eat three and stop

effects.log: Three cups. The Hunger sulks at the other six, but you walk home on your own feet.

choices.text: Send the crane back with a polite refusal

effects.log: You fold the crane a little neater than it came and send it home.

events.text: The Widow comes to you with white in her hair. "There is nothing left in my jars that can harm you," she says, "and that frightens me more than any rival ever did." She holds out the book of her nine recipes.
events.arc: The Widow of Black Reed Marsh

choices.text: Burn the book together

effects.log: The smoke is green and smells of plums. She weeps a little and says she feels lighter.

choices.text: Keep the book, and her secret

effects.log: You keep the book. The Hunger reads it at night like a menu.

choices.text: Ask her to brew a tenth, one that heals

effects.log: It takes her a year. The tenth cup tastes of nothing at all, and your old cough is gone.

events.text: A shy pupil of the Widow's arrives with a sealed jar: the antidote to the seventh cup, perfected at last, years too late to matter. "She said you would want it anyway," the pupil says, "for the next fool."
events.arc: The Widow of Black Reed Marsh

choices.text: Keep it for the next fool

effects.log: The jar sits on your shelf, a small green promise.

choices.text: Drink it, for the old ache in your belly

effects.log: The ache you stopped noticing goes away, and you notice.

choices.text: Feed it to the Hunger to see what happens

effects.log: The Hunger eats the cure as happily as the poison. It has no principles.

events.text: A jar of plum wine arrives with a note in green ink: "Coward. Unpoisoned. Possibly." The Hunger leans toward it like a dog to a butcher's door. You are almost sure the Widow is joking.
events.arc: The Widow of Black Reed Marsh

choices.text: Pour it out on the plum tree, to be safe

effects.log: The tree is only better for it. You write back: "Possibly coward."

choices.text: Give it to the innkeeper next door

effects.log: The innkeeper is fine. The innkeeper is very cheerful for a week.

events.text: Iron-Arm Gu has sparred with you every tenth day for years and loses every time with a grin. Today he goes down hard, and the Hunger rises like a tide: Ding. Defeated opponent. Devour?
events.arc: The One You Would Not Eat

choices.text: Refuse, and help him up

effects.log: The Hunger gnaws you for a week out of spite. Gu buys the noodles.

choices.text: Take only a sip of his qi

effects.log: Gu feels tired for a month and never knows why. You know.

choices.text: Stop sparring with him

effects.log: You tell Gu you are busy. He comes by anyway with a jug and talks about his tomatoes.

events.text: Gu comes home from an escort job with his chest strapped, his qi leaking out of him like steam from a cracked pot. The Hunger can taste it from across the yard. The physician says rest; the Hunger says waste.
events.arc: The One You Would Not Eat

choices.text: Push your own qi into him instead

effects.log: It is the first time the Hunger has ever had to give something back. It howls. Gu sleeps.

choices.text: Sit with him and hold the Hunger down

ok.log: All night you sit on your hands, and by dawn the leak has closed on its own.

fail.log: You last until midnight. A little of his qi drifts into you before you can leave the room.

choices.text: Stay away until he heals

effects.log: You send soup. You do not trust yourself with more than soup.

events.text: Years later, over the old noodles, Gu says it without looking up: "I know what you are. I knew the first day you helped me up." He pushes the last dumpling across the table to you.
events.arc: The One You Would Not Eat

choices.text: Tell him everything

effects.log: He listens to all of it and says the Hunger should come to his tomato harvest. It has never been invited anywhere.

choices.text: Eat the dumpling and say nothing

effects.log: It is the only thing you have eaten in years that the Hunger did not want a share of.

events.text: The villages under Pine Ridge have lost four oxen and a mule to a white tiger with a spirit core, the kind that glows through its fur at night. The headman offers forty taels. The Hunger offers no opinion, only a growl.
events.arc: The White Tiger of Pine Ridge

choices.text: Hunt the tiger

ok.log: The fight in the snow is short and loud, and the tiger lies still. (40 taels)

fail.log: The tiger throws you down a slope and goes back to sleep. The villagers carry you home.

choices.text: Track it first and learn its ways

effects.log: Three days in the snow: it is old, it is lame, and it only hunts what wanders into its valley.

choices.text: Tell the headman to fence the valley

effects.log: The fence costs the village a month of work. The oxen stop disappearing.

events.text: The tiger's core lies before you, glowing like a lantern in the snow, worth a sect elder's ransom to an alchemist. Ding. Beast essence detected. The Hunger is very, very interested.
events.arc: The White Tiger of Pine Ridge

choices.text: Devour the core

effects.log: The Hunger eats the winter itself. For a year you never feel cold.

choices.text: Sell it to the alchemist in town

effects.log: The alchemist counts out the silver with shaking hands. (300 taels)

choices.text: Bury it on the ridge where the tiger lived

effects.log: The snow over the grave never quite settles. The villagers say the ridge is lucky now.

events.text: Tracking the tiger to its den you find why it hunts: two cubs, thin as rakes. The tiger watches you from the rocks and does not move. The Hunger, for once, is quiet.
events.arc: The White Tiger of Pine Ridge

choices.text: Leave the village half your dried meat, for the oxen they lost

effects.log: You pay the headman for an ox and tell him the tiger is gone. (-20 taels)

choices.text: Bring the cubs fish all winter

effects.log: By spring the cubs follow you to the river. The village pretends not to see.

choices.text: Leave them be

effects.log: You walk down the ridge. Behind you, in the den, something purrs.

events.text: The Mid-Autumn fair holds a dumpling-eating contest: the prize is a carp lantern and twenty taels. The Hunger has never cared for food. Ding. It would like you to know that it does not care now, either.

choices.text: Enter anyway

ok.log: Sixty-one dumplings. The carp lantern is yours. The Hunger is baffled. (20 taels)

fail.log: Forty-two dumplings, third place and a long night.

choices.text: Cheer for the butcher's daughter Ma Lan

effects.log: Ma Lan wins with seventy and waves the lantern at you.

choices.text: Watch from the wall and eat nothing

effects.log: You learn that a crowd cheering is a kind of food too.

events.text: The old cook who rolled the contest dumplings, Granny Shen, finds you at her stall. "You eat like something inside you is not hungry for dumplings," she says. "I had a husband like that. I fed him anyway."

choices.text: Ask what she fed him

effects.log: Millet porridge with ginger, every morning, forty years. She writes it down for you.

choices.text: Pay her for a bowl a week

effects.log: Every seventh day, a bowl that tastes of somebody caring. (-15 taels)

choices.text: Laugh it off

effects.log: She laughs too, and does not believe a word you say.

events.text: Granny Shen's stall is shut and her grandson is selling the cart. Before she died she left a jar of ginger with your name on it. That night the Hunger is quieter than it has been in years. Ding, it says, small. Missing: one cook.

choices.text: Learn to make the porridge yourself

effects.log: Your first pot is a disaster. Your fortieth is hers.

choices.text: Pay for her grave stone

effects.log: A small stone, carved with a ladle. (-40 taels)

events.text: Abbot Huiming of Hollow Bell Temple has eaten one bowl of rice a day for sixty years. He looks at you as if he can see the Hunger sitting behind your ribs. "Forty-nine days," he offers. "Fast with us, and see who is master."
events.arc: Forty-Nine Days at Hollow Bell Temple

choices.text: Fast the forty-nine days

ok.log: On the forty-ninth day the Hunger sits down and folds its hands. It has never done that.

fail.log: On the thirtieth day you are found in the kitchen with a radish. The abbot is kind about it.

choices.text: Sweep the courtyard for a season instead

effects.log: The broom is older than the abbot. Your hands learn it.

choices.text: Decline: the Hunger is not his to tame

effects.log: Huiming bows. "Then feed it well," he says, "or it will choose the menu."

events.text: A runner comes down from the mountain: Abbot Huiming is dying. When you arrive he takes your wrist. "There is a little qi left in me," he says. "Do not let it go into the ground. Take it." The Hunger stands up.
events.arc: Forty-Nine Days at Hollow Bell Temple

choices.text: Devour what he offers

effects.log: It tastes of sixty years of plain rice. It is the best thing the Hunger has ever eaten.

choices.text: Let it go back to the mountain

effects.log: His qi rises like incense into the pines, and you hold his hand while it does.

choices.text: Ask him for a lesson instead

effects.log: He laughs, coughs, and spends his last evening teaching you to breathe slower.

events.text: A pawnshop in the river district keeps a rusted sabre wrapped in chains, because it hums. The owner swears it once drank a customer's qi through the glove. When you walk in, the sabre and the Hunger both go very still.

choices.text: Buy the sabre

effects.log: The owner throws in the chains for free and locks the door behind you. (-60 taels)

choices.text: Ask to hold it, just once

ok.log: It bites; the Hunger bites back. The sabre lets go first, and the owner gives it to you to be rid of it.

fail.log: It drinks a mouthful of your qi before you drop it. The Hunger is furious for a month.

choices.text: Leave it to someone else

effects.log: Two hungers in one room is one too many.

events.text: The sabre has rust on it still, but it no longer hums at you. It hums at the Hunger, low and constant, like two dogs who share a yard. Ding. Devour the blade's spirit?

choices.text: Devour it

effects.log: The spirit is old and bitter. Afterwards the sabre is only iron, and sharper than ever.

choices.text: Let them keep each other company

effects.log: You sleep with the sabre by the bed. The Hunger rises slower that year.

choices.text: Sink it in the deepest well in town

effects.log: The well water tastes of iron for a while, and then of nothing.

events.text: A sabre master of the Five Tigers school, an elderly man called Bo Ren, sees the rusted sabre at your hip and stops in the road. "My teacher's," he says. "It ate him slowly. How is it not eating you?"

choices.text: Give it back to his school

effects.log: He carries it home in both arms. The Hunger misses its friend.

choices.text: Keep it and show him why

effects.log: He watches the two hungers hum at each other and leaves shaking his head.

events.text: The fishermen of Mirror Lake say an old dragon sleeps in the cave under the falls, coiled on a bed of pearls. Ding. The voice has gone breathless. "Host. A dragon's nest. Do you know what a dragon's nest pays?"

choices.text: Swim in and sign at the nest

ok.log: Your palm on the warm scales, a ding like a temple bell, and out again before the eye opens.

fail.log: One eye opens. You are out of the lake before you know you have moved, without your boots.

choices.text: Sign at the cave mouth, to be safe

effects.log: "The doorstep," the voice says, wounded. "Of a dragon. Very well."

choices.text: Bring the dragon a gift of carp first

effects.log: A basket of carp at the falls. Something under the water accepts it. (-10 taels)

events.text: A woman in pearl-grey robes is waiting by your door, eyes the yellow of old amber. "Someone," she says, "has been writing their name on my bed." The voice says nothing at all, very loudly.

choices.text: Apologise and offer to sign her into the register

effects.log: She has never been written in anything. She likes it far too much.

choices.text: Bargain: a share of the reward, every year

effects.log: She takes the silver and a promise. Mirror Lake is calm all year. (-30 taels)

choices.text: Stand your ground

ok.log: She tests you once, laughs like rain and goes home.

fail.log: You wake up in a reed bed half a li downstream.

events.text: Each year's end now the dragon in grey comes up out of Mirror Lake to watch you sign in, which she calls "our little ceremony". This year she brings a pearl. "For the streak," she says. "Do not break it."

choices.text: Take the pearl

effects.log: It is warm in your palm and never cools.

choices.text: Ask her to sign in with you

effects.log: Two palms on the stone. The voice stamps a Vermilion Double Seal and pretends it was its idea.

events.text: Magistrate Cao has taxed the salt villages to the bone, and his study, the voice notes, has never once been signed in. "High walls," it says, "guard dogs, corrupt ledgers. A very rich place, Host. Spiritually."

choices.text: Climb in at midnight and sign

ok.log: Ding, very quietly. On the desk, under your hand, lies the second ledger, the true one.

fail.log: The dogs are better than the walls. You spend a year in the county cell.

choices.text: Sign in on the street outside his gate

effects.log: "The pavement," the voice sighs. "Of a villain."

choices.text: Go to the salt villages instead

effects.log: You sign in at a salt pan. It pays very little and the women give you fish.

events.text: You know where the true ledger is: under the inkstone, in the drawer with the broken lock. The voice has taken an interest in justice, or at least in a second visit.

choices.text: Take the ledger to the prefect

effects.log: The prefect reads it in one sitting. Cao is gone by spring.

choices.text: Make Cao pay the villages back, quietly

effects.log: One letter under his pillow. The villages get their silver and you get a thank-you fee. (80 taels)

choices.text: Leave it: not your business

effects.log: You sign elsewhere. The voice mutters about wasted potential.

events.text: The salt villages hold a feast with Cao's old chairs in the square. They ask you to sign in at the head of the table, "where the thief used to sit". The voice is so happy it dings twice.

choices.text: Sign in at the head of the table

effects.log: The rarest place in the register: a seat given back.

choices.text: Give the seat to the oldest salt woman

effects.log: She sits in it all evening and will not get up for anybody.

events.text: By the road out of town there is a plum tree, and under it a blind tea seller, old Auntie Xu, who hears you sign in there one year's end and says: "Ten years at a gate, they say. Why not ten years at a tree?"

choices.text: Promise her ten years

effects.log: She pours you tea for free and tells you the plum blossom is late this year.

choices.text: Buy her tea and move on

effects.log: Good tea. You sign somewhere grander next year. (-2 taels)

choices.text: Ask why she sits here

effects.log: Her son walked down this road forty years ago. She likes to hear who comes back.

events.text: Five year-ends at the plum tree. Auntie Xu knows your step from a hundred paces now. The voice has started calling the tree "our tree", and Auntie Xu has started saving you the good cup.

choices.text: Bring her a warm coat this winter

effects.log: She says it is too fine for a tea seller and wears it every day. (-12 taels)

choices.text: Read her the letters people leave at the tree

effects.log: Lovers, debtors, a child who lost a kite. She laughs at all of them.

events.text: The tenth year's end. The stool under the plum tree is empty, and a neighbour says Auntie Xu went in the autumn, "wearing that coat". The voice is silent. Then, softly: Ding. Ten years at one place.

choices.text: Sign in, and keep the streak going

effects.log: You sign. Then you sit on the stool a long time, listening to the road.

choices.text: Leave her stool for someone else to sit on

effects.log: Next year a child sells plums there. You buy them all.

events.text: At the spring kite festival a kite maker flies a kite big enough to carry a child. Ding. The voice wonders aloud, in the tone of a scholar with a thesis, whether the sky counts as a place one may sign in.

choices.text: Ride the kite up and find out

ok.log: Fifty feet up, a ding like a wind chime. The voice is overcome. The sky counts.

fail.log: The string snaps at twenty feet. You land in the noodle tent, which does not count.

choices.text: Help the kite maker sell kites

effects.log: You sell thirty kites by telling everyone a ghost might ride one. (15 taels)

choices.text: Tell the voice the sky is not a place

effects.log: It sulks until summer and calls you "the ground-bound one".

events.text: The voice has a new list: a boat on the open sea, the top of a pagoda in a storm, the back of a running horse. "For science," it says. The kite maker, Old Sima, wants to build a bigger kite.

choices.text: Help Old Sima build a kite for two

effects.log: Two of you, a hundred feet up, and the whole town looking up with their mouths open. (-25 taels)

choices.text: Try the running horse

ok.log: Standing on a galloping horse with one palm on its back. The register writes: a place that moves.

fail.log: The horse disagrees with science.

choices.text: Refuse: one sky is enough

effects.log: The voice says you have no sense of adventure, and also that it is relieved.

events.text: Scholar Ouyang Ji is compiling a gazetteer of the empire's forgotten places, and has heard that someone signs their name, so to speak, in strange spots. He would like to follow you for a year with a brush and a donkey.

choices.text: Let him come

effects.log: The donkey is called Confucius. The voice is jealous of the scholar inside a week.

choices.text: Give him a list of places instead

effects.log: He thanks you nine times and leaves with the list held to his chest.

choices.text: Tell him you do nothing of the kind

effects.log: He does not believe you, but he is too polite to say so.

events.text: A year on the road with Ouyang Ji: a ruined beacon tower, a well-known ghost bridge, a mill where three rivers meet. His book is half done. He asks, a little embarrassed, if he may put you in it.

choices.text: Yes, under your own name

effects.log: The chapter is called "A Traveller Who Stands Still". People start asking you to sign in at their shops.

choices.text: Yes, but as "a nameless traveller"

effects.log: The nameless traveller becomes a small legend. Nobody suspects you.

choices.text: Pay for the printing

effects.log: Two hundred copies, with a donkey on the cover. (-50 taels)

events.text: A copy of the Gazetteer of Odd Places reaches a governor, who adds a line to the province's maps at every place in it. Ding. The voice is quiet a while. "We are on the maps, Host," it says at last. "Our register."

choices.text: Sign in at the first place in the book, again

effects.log: The ruined beacon tower, a new stone on it: a palm print, carved by someone who read the book.

choices.text: Write Ouyang Ji a long letter

effects.log: He writes back twenty pages and a sketch of the donkey, older now.

events.text: At the Emperor's birthday the palace opens its outer court to the people for one night. The voice has gone very formal. "The jade steps below the Dragon Throne, Host. Nine of them. Only nine people in history have stood there."
events.arc: The Steps of the Dragon Throne

choices.text: Slip past the guards to the steps

ok.log: A palm on cold jade, a ding like a bronze bell, and a very old eunuch watching you from behind a pillar.

fail.log: Nine steps; you reach the second. Two years in the capital cells.

choices.text: Sign in at the outer court with the crowd

effects.log: Ten thousand people and lanterns. The voice says it counts as a little bit.

choices.text: Watch the fireworks instead

effects.log: The voice sighs once and then watches with you.

events.text: A letter in vermilion ink, no name: "The second step from the top is cracked. Mind it. A friend from behind the pillar." Then, a month later: an invitation to tea with Eunuch Lin of the Hall of Records.
events.arc: The Steps of the Dragon Throne

choices.text: Go to tea

effects.log: He has kept a register of his own for sixty years: everyone who climbed those steps. You are the tenth.

choices.text: Burn the letter and lie low

effects.log: Nobody comes. You still flinch at vermilion ink.

events.text: Eunuch Lin is dying in a small room behind the Hall of Records. He asks you to do one thing: sign in here, in his plain room, so that it is written somewhere that the room existed.
events.arc: The Steps of the Dragon Throne

choices.text: Sign in at his bedside

effects.log: Ding, softly. He smiles. "Ten," he says. "A good number to end on."

choices.text: Take his register to keep

effects.log: Sixty years of names in a small neat hand. The voice reads it with you every year.

events.text: Ding. Hidden talent detected: not among your disciples, but in your kitchen. Little Hong, fourteen, is chopping leeks, and every slice is the same width as the last, to the hair. The System is very excited.

choices.text: Make her a disciple today

effects.log: The cook is furious. Little Hong holds a wooden sword as if it were a cleaver, perfectly.

choices.text: Ask her what she wants

effects.log: "To cook," she says. "Mostly. But I would like to know what this is."

choices.text: Leave her in the kitchen

effects.log: The leeks stay perfect. The System sulks.

events.text: Little Hong has grown fast. The System's appraisal reads [Heaven-Cut Wrist]. The other disciples are jealous, and the cook still sends for her when there are leeks. The sect tournament is next month.

choices.text: Enter her in the tournament

ok.log: She wins in nine cuts and bows to the cook in the crowd.

fail.log: She loses the final, to an elder's nephew. She goes to the kitchen and chops for an hour.

choices.text: Let her split her days: kitchen and yard

effects.log: Mornings the sword, evenings the stove. She is happier than anyone in the hall.

events.text: Little Hong asks to sit with you at the cook's old stove. "I want to cook," she says, "and also learn the sword. Can I?" The System has no box for this, and says so.

choices.text: Give her both

effects.log: She takes the sword in the morning and the soup pot at night. Nobody in the hall eats badly again.

choices.text: Give her the kitchen

effects.log: She runs it like a general. The leeks are still perfect.

events.text: Years on, Hong leaves the sect with your blessing and opens a noodle shop at the foot of the mountain called The Perfect Leek. Every lord of every sect that visits ends up there. The System files it as [Sect Outpost].

choices.text: Eat there every month

effects.log: She never lets you pay. You leave the silver under the bowl anyway.

choices.text: Send new disciples there to learn patience

effects.log: They come back able to cut a leek. Some of them come back able to cut anything.

events.text: A summer storm, and at midnight the roof of your sect's Scripture Hall comes down with a noise like a giant clearing his throat. Ding. [Sect Facility Damaged]. The manuals are under the beams and the rain is coming in.
events.arc: The Night the Scripture Hall Fell

choices.text: Lift the beams yourself

ok.log: You hold the main beam while the disciples carry out every scroll. Nobody sleeps; nobody is hurt.

fail.log: The beam wins. The disciples save half the scrolls while you lie in the mud.

choices.text: Rouse the disciples and form a chain

effects.log: Forty disciples pass scrolls hand to hand in the rain. It becomes the night they all talk about.

choices.text: Save the founder's manual first

effects.log: One manual saved, dry inside your robe. The rest is wet paper by morning.

events.text: Old Carpenter Mo offers to rebuild the Scripture Hall: properly, with cedar, in a year, for three hundred taels; or cheaply, with pine, in a month, for eighty. He looks at the sky as he speaks. He has opinions about pine.
events.arc: The Night the Scripture Hall Fell

choices.text: Cedar, properly

effects.log: A year of sawdust and a hall that will stand two hundred years. (-300 taels)

choices.text: Pine, quickly

effects.log: A month later the disciples are reading again. Mo does not come to the opening. (-80 taels)

choices.text: Have the disciples build it with Mo

effects.log: It takes two years and is a little crooked. Every disciple knows which beam is theirs.

events.text: Another storm, worse than the last. In the dark you stand at the window and watch the new Scripture Hall take the wind, rain hammering the cedar shingles. The System waits with you.
events.arc: The Night the Scripture Hall Fell

choices.text: Go out and check it at dawn

effects.log: Not a tile out of place. Mo, eighty now, comes up the mountain just to look at it.

choices.text: Sleep: you trust it

effects.log: You sleep through the whole storm. It is still there.

events.text: Another storm, worse than the last. The pine hall groans all night, and at dawn the east wall is leaning like a drunk at a wedding. Old Carpenter Mo, eighty now, is waiting at the gate with his tools.
events.arc: The Night the Scripture Hall Fell

choices.text: Pay Mo to do it properly this time

effects.log: He says nothing about pine. Not one word. It is worse. (-200 taels)

choices.text: Prop it up and hope

effects.log: The disciples call it the Leaning Hall. Visitors come to see it.

events.text: Ding. [Mission Failed: Escort to Hongyan Pass]. Three of your disciples took a salt caravan into the hills a week ago and have not come back, and now the snow has closed the road. The merchant is already asking for his money.
events.arc: The Salt Escort in the Snow

choices.text: Go after them yourself

ok.log: You find them in a shepherd's hut, half frozen, the salt carts still guarded. The bandits in the pass go home.

fail.log: You find them, but the bandits find you all. Everyone comes home; the salt does not.

choices.text: Pay the merchant back and send a search party

effects.log: The search party brings them home in spring, thin and alive. (-120 taels)

choices.text: Wait for the snow to clear

effects.log: Two come home in spring. The third, Tan Yu, stays in a village that took them in.

events.text: The three disciples from the snow, Fen, Old Zhou and little Tan Yu, ask to see you. They want to found a branch hall at Hongyan Pass, by the shepherd's hut, so no caravan is ever lost there again.
events.arc: The Salt Escort in the Snow

choices.text: Grant it, with your blessing

effects.log: The Pass Hall is three rooms and a bell. Caravans start asking for it by name.

choices.text: Refuse: they are needed here

effects.log: They stay. Every winter they look at the hills.

events.text: The Martial Alliance sends Inspector Gongsun to rank the young sects of the province. He has a little ivory abacus and a face like a closed door. Ding. [Sect Goal Updated: Impress the Inspector].

choices.text: Show him the training yard at dawn

ok.log: Sixty disciples in step, and one beat in the abacus. You think it was a good beat.

fail.log: A disciple sneezes in the middle of the form, and then everyone is out of step.

choices.text: Feed him very well

effects.log: He eats three bowls and writes nothing. (-30 taels)

choices.text: Show him the sect as it really is

effects.log: The leaking well, the old rice, the disciple who is good at nothing but laughing.

events.text: The Alliance ranking arrives. Below it, in Inspector Gongsun's hand, a line nobody else will read: "The disciple who laughed at the well. Keep that one, whatever else you lose."

choices.text: Find out why

effects.log: The inspector once had a sect of his own. Nobody laughed in it.

choices.text: Make that disciple the hall's greeter

effects.log: Visitors leave in a better mood. Recruitment rises.

events.text: Gongsun returns three years later, older and less like a door. He does not bring the abacus. He would like, he says, simply to sit in your training yard for a morning.

choices.text: Let him watch

effects.log: He sits on the steps all morning and goes away looking ten years younger.

choices.text: Ask him to teach a class

effects.log: He teaches the disciples to count without an abacus. They hate it and love him.

events.text: You have no sect, no hall and no disciples, only a System that keeps showing you an empty roster. Then a beggar child called Pebble starts following you through the market at ten paces, copying the way you walk.

choices.text: Give Pebble a job carrying your things

effects.log: Ding. [Roster: 1]. Pebble carries one bag and is unbearably proud of it.

choices.text: Buy Pebble a meal and move on

effects.log: Pebble eats, bows, and keeps following anyway. (-3 taels)

choices.text: Shoo Pebble off

effects.log: Pebble goes. The roster stays empty a while longer.

events.text: Pebble has learned three stances by watching you train behind the woodpile. Badly, but all three. The System's appraisal hovers: [Hidden Talent: locked]. It will not say more until there is a sect.

choices.text: Start teaching Pebble properly

effects.log: Mornings, behind the woodpile. Your first lesson, your first student.

choices.text: Find Pebble a place in a real sect

effects.log: A sect in the next town takes Pebble in. You miss the footsteps behind you.

events.text: Pebble, taller now, sits on the woodpile and asks what you will call the sect, when you have one. "Because I'm the first," Pebble says. "I want to be able to tell people."

choices.text: Let Pebble name it

effects.log: The name is terrible. You keep it anyway.

choices.text: Promise to found it within three years

effects.log: Ding. [Sect Goal: Found the sect]. Pebble holds you to it.

events.text: In the market square Old Pang spins nine plates on nine poles while hopping on one foot, and never drops one. The Mirror flickers. Ding. [Technique Seen: Nine Plates Footwork (common)]. Copy?

choices.text: Copy it

effects.log: The footwork settles into your legs like a song you always knew.

choices.text: Pay Old Pang and watch the whole show

effects.log: You copy it anyway, but at least you paid. (-2 taels)

choices.text: Look away: it is his living

effects.log: The Mirror is bewildered. You buy a candied haw instead.

events.text: You use the plate-spinner's footwork in a real fight and slip a spear thrust by a hair. Afterwards an old voice in the crowd says, "Hop on the left foot, not the right. You dropped a plate there." It is Old Pang.

choices.text: Ask him to correct you properly

effects.log: He corrects you for an hour and charges a bowl of noodles.

choices.text: Apologise for taking it without asking

effects.log: "Everybody takes it," he says. "You are the first to use it well."

choices.text: Deny it was his

effects.log: He shrugs and walks off on one foot. The crowd laughs at you.

events.text: Old Pang can no longer hop. He asks you to do the nine plates at his last show in the square, "so they see it was never a trick". The Mirror shows the copy at full power, gold at the edges.

choices.text: Do the show

ok.log: Nine plates. Not one drops. Old Pang cries and pretends it is the dust.

fail.log: One plate drops. Old Pang laughs louder than anyone and catches it.

choices.text: Teach his grandson instead

effects.log: A month of lessons. The boy drops a hundred plates and then none.

events.text: You win a duel with a cloud-step palm you copied two years ago from a fight you watched in the rain. In the crowd an elder of the Azure Cloud Sect, Elder Fang, has gone white. Ding. [Warning: Owner of Secret Technique Present].

choices.text: Walk up to Elder Fang and bow

effects.log: He does not bow back. He asks where you learned it, very quietly.

choices.text: Leave town by the back road

effects.log: You are gone before evening. The Azure Cloud Sect has a long memory.

choices.text: Bluff that it is your own invention

ok.log: He almost believes you. Almost is enough for today.

fail.log: He names the third move before you make it. The crowd goes very quiet.

events.text: In a teahouse Elder Fang hears you out: the rain, the duel, the Mirror. Then he says, "That palm killed my teacher's brother. It was the wrong man who used it that day. Show me what you do with it."

choices.text: Spar with him, holding nothing back

ok.log: He stops the bout with a laugh. "Better than my nephews," he says.

fail.log: He beats you with his own palm, done right. You learn more from losing than from copying.

choices.text: Swear never to use it again

effects.log: The Mirror greys the copy out. Elder Fang pays for the tea.

events.text: A letter with the Azure Cloud seal: Elder Fang has told the sect that the cloud-step palm has "a guest in the world, with my leave". Enclosed, in his hand, a fourth move nobody outside the sect has ever seen.

choices.text: Learn the fourth move

effects.log: The Mirror cannot copy a letter. You learn this one the slow way, and it is yours.

choices.text: Send it back unread

effects.log: He writes back one word: "Fool." Then a second letter: "Thank you."

events.text: Two young men in Azure Cloud blue are waiting at the ferry. "Elder Fang would like his palm back," says one, "and he does not much care whether we bring it in your hands or in a basket."

choices.text: Fight them

ok.log: The fight is short. They go home wet, and the Azure Cloud Sect will remember.

fail.log: They beat you at the river and leave you on the jetty.

choices.text: Go with them to the sect

effects.log: Elder Fang makes you kneel a day in the courtyard, then teaches you why the palm must never be used in anger.

events.text: Every dawn a blind fisherman, Grandfather Lu, casts his net on the river in a circle so perfect that the water rings. The Mirror tries. Ding. [Copy Failed: No Technique Found]. It tries again. Same answer.
events.arc: The Cast That Would Not Copy

choices.text: Ask Grandfather Lu to teach you

effects.log: "Teach what?" he says. "I just throw it." He gives you a net anyway.

choices.text: Watch him every morning for a month

effects.log: Thirty dawns, thirty perfect circles. The Mirror grows quieter each day.

choices.text: Shrug and move on

effects.log: Somewhere downstream the water rings, every morning, without you.

events.text: You have thrown Grandfather Lu's net four hundred times. You have caught eleven fish, three boots and a crab who will not let go. The Mirror shows nothing. Grandfather Lu sits on the bank, listening and grinning.
events.arc: The Cast That Would Not Copy

choices.text: Keep throwing

ok.log: On the five hundredth throw, the water rings. Grandfather Lu claps once.

fail.log: Your arms grow very strong and the net stays lopsided.

choices.text: Ask the Mirror why it cannot copy this

effects.log: After a long while it answers: [Technique requires: forty years].

events.text: Grandfather Lu's net hangs on your wall now. He told you before he went that his circle came from throwing it the day his wife died and not stopping. Every dawn, when you throw it, the Mirror stays dark, as if it is listening.
events.arc: The Cast That Would Not Copy

choices.text: Throw it at dawn on the river

effects.log: The water rings. It is the only thing you know that the Mirror did not give you.

choices.text: Give the net to a fisher child

effects.log: The child throws a terrible circle and laughs. You tell them to keep going for forty years.

events.text: At a travelling opera the clown, Little Jade Monkey, imitates everyone in the audience, and then imitates you, and his hands do your copied techniques, all three, perfectly. The Mirror flashes red. Ding. [Rival Copier].

choices.text: Challenge him after the show

ok.log: He copies every move you make, so you make one you have never made. He bows out laughing.

fail.log: He beats you with your own palm and then takes a bow over you.

choices.text: Laugh with the crowd

effects.log: It is a very good impression. You hate how good it is.

choices.text: Copy him back

effects.log: The Mirror copies a man copying you. Something in it creaks.

events.text: Little Jade Monkey finds you at your inn with two cups of wine. "I have no mirror," he says, "only eyes, and a troupe that eats on what they see. Teach me one move that is truly yours, and I will stop doing you."

choices.text: Show him the one move that is yours

effects.log: He learns it in a night and never performs it. He says some things are not for the stage.

choices.text: Refuse, and make him swear off you

effects.log: He swears, and does an impression of you swearing, and you have to laugh.

choices.text: Join the troupe for a season

effects.log: A season of painted faces down the canals. The Mirror copies a hundred dances, none of them dangerous.

events.text: A boy from the tannery has watched you train for weeks. He wants to learn the sabre turn you use, the one the Mirror copied from a dead bandit chief. Ding. [Note: Teaching a Copy is Untested].

choices.text: Teach him

effects.log: You try. Your copy does not know how it is done, only that it is done. You have to work it out.

choices.text: Teach him something you learned the slow way

effects.log: A plain stance, the first you ever learned. He hates it. He keeps at it.

choices.text: Send him to a proper school

effects.log: You pay his first month at a sabre school. (-10 taels)

events.text: Working it out for the tannery boy, you take the sabre turn apart move by move, and find the place where the bandit chief had it wrong, and fix it. The Mirror looks at your hands again. Ding. [Copy Exceeds Original].

choices.text: Keep teaching the boy the fixed turn

effects.log: He learns it right from the start. He will never know there was a wrong way.

choices.text: Write the fixed turn down for the sabre schools

effects.log: Three schools copy your pages. The Mirror finds this very funny.

events.text: [Daily Quest] Eat ten steamed buns. Reward: 50 EXP. Time limit: today. Below it, the window adds in smaller letters: (Penalty for failure: mild disappointment.) Auntie Wu's bun stall is just opening.

choices.text: Buy ten buns from Auntie Wu

effects.log: Ten buns, one after another. Auntie Wu is impressed and slightly alarmed. (-2 taels)

choices.text: Eat ten buns but share each one with the street children

effects.log: [Quest Partly Complete: half-buns detected]. The children do not mind. (-4 taels)

choices.text: Ignore the quest

effects.log: [Quest Failed]. You feel mildly disappointed, exactly as promised.

events.text: [Daily Quest] Eat ten steamed buns. Again. It is the fourth time this month. Auntie Wu now has your ten in a basket before you reach the stall, and has started trying new fillings on you.

choices.text: Try the new chive filling

effects.log: It is wonderful. [Hidden Bonus: Discerning Palate].

choices.text: Ask Auntie Wu about her bun stall

effects.log: Thirty years, two sons gone to the army, one stall. She is behind on the rent.

events.text: Auntie Wu's landlord wants her stall for a pickle shop. The window offers nothing; no quest, no reward. It seems to be waiting to see what you do without one.

choices.text: Pay her rent for the year

effects.log: [Hidden Quest Complete: Buns for Life]. Auntie Wu gives you ten buns a day, forever. (-40 taels)

choices.text: Have a word with the landlord

ok.log: The landlord finds he likes buns more than pickles. The stall stays.

fail.log: He does not like buns. You help Auntie Wu move the stall two streets over.

events.text: On a stormy coast road a blue window opens that you have never seen before: [Hidden Quest: The Lantern That Never Goes Out]. Ahead, on the rocks, an old beacon keeper, Grandfather Bao, is fighting the wind for his flame.
events.arc: Hidden Quest: The Lantern That Never Goes Out

choices.text: Help him keep the beacon lit

ok.log: All night you shield the flame with your back. At dawn a fishing fleet comes home.

fail.log: The flame goes out twice. Twice you light it again. Some boats come home late.

choices.text: Ask the window what the reward is

effects.log: [Reward: unknown]. You walk on. The beacon is dark behind you by midnight.

events.text: [Hidden Quest: Stage 2]. Grandfather Bao's oil is running out and the oil merchant in town will not sell to an old man with no silver. The keeper has been burning his furniture. The window shows one word: [Choose].
events.arc: Hidden Quest: The Lantern That Never Goes Out

choices.text: Buy the oil yourself

effects.log: Two barrels on a cart up the cliff road. (-30 taels)

choices.text: Go to the fishing village and ask

effects.log: Every family gives a cup of oil. It is enough for a winter.

choices.text: Leave it: it is not your coast

effects.log: [Quest Abandoned]. The window does not mention it again.

events.text: [Hidden Quest: Final Stage]. Grandfather Bao is too old to climb the tower. He holds the lantern out to you. "Not forever," he says. "Only until someone takes it from you."
events.arc: Hidden Quest: The Lantern That Never Goes Out

choices.text: Keep the beacon a year and train a keeper

effects.log: [Hidden Quest Complete]. A fisher girl takes the lantern from you in spring. [Title: Keeper of the Light].

choices.text: Find the village a young keeper now

effects.log: A boy who has watched the tower all his life. Bao teaches him for the rest of his own.

events.text: Ding. Level up. [Unassigned stat points: 1]. Tomorrow you fight the Wolf of Three Valleys at the county tournament. The night after, you have promised to sing at your friend Ru Yi's wedding. The cursor blinks.

choices.text: Put it in Body

effects.log: Your arms feel like oak. Your singing voice feels like oak too.

choices.text: Put it in Charm

effects.log: You feel like you could sing to a stone and make it cry.

choices.text: Leave it unassigned for an emergency

effects.log: [1 point held]. The window is clearly judging you.

events.text: The tournament. The Wolf of Three Valleys is very large and very confident, and cracks his knuckles at you across the ring. Somewhere behind him in the stands you see Ru Yi waving a red scarf.

choices.text: Fight him

ok.log: He goes down in the second exchange. You are very glad of whatever you chose.

fail.log: He throws you out of the ring. [EXP for effort: 30].

choices.text: Spend the held point mid-fight

effects.log: Ding, in the middle of a punch. The Wolf never sees it coming.

choices.text: Bow out and save your voice

effects.log: The crowd boos. Ru Yi does not.

events.text: Ru Yi's wedding. Two hundred guests, red lanterns over every table, a pipa player tuning in the corner and a cup of tea in your hand. The whole courtyard turns to look. It is your turn to sing.

choices.text: Sing

ok.log: Even the bride's grandmother cries. [Hidden Achievement: Wedding Singer].

fail.log: It is terrible. Everybody loves it anyway, because it is terrible.

choices.text: Recite a poem instead

effects.log: Ru Yi laughs so hard that the groom has to hold the cup.

events.text: A neighbour's rooster has woken you at the fourth watch for a year. This morning you lose your temper and throw a slipper at it. You miss. You hit the coop. The coop falls down. Ding. [Title Earned: Destroyer of Chickens].

choices.text: Rebuild the coop

effects.log: It takes a day. The rooster watches every nail and crows at the last one.

choices.text: Try to remove the title

effects.log: [Titles cannot be removed]. It is shown above your status, in red.

choices.text: Pay the neighbour for the coop

effects.log: He takes the silver and says the chickens will remember. (-6 taels)

events.text: The title has a bonus. [Destroyer of Chickens: +10% intimidation against poultry]. You learn this when a flock of geese at the river parts before you like a court before a magistrate.

choices.text: Use it to cross the goose farm on the short road

effects.log: The famous geese of Elm Bend let you pass. The farmer has never seen it before.

choices.text: Hide it behind a better title

ok.log: A rescue at the ford earns you [Title: Bridge Guardian]. You set it as your display title at once.

fail.log: The next title you earn is [Title: Still Destroyer of Chickens].

events.text: The neighbour's old rooster dies of a great age, and the neighbour, to your surprise, asks you to bury it, "since you two had history". Ding. [Title Evolving...]

choices.text: Bury it under the plum tree with honours

effects.log: [Title Evolved: Friend of Chickens]. The hens follow you around the yard for a year.

choices.text: Refuse: you have your pride

effects.log: [Title Unchanged]. The hens glare at you from the fence.

events.text: The window shows other people's levels now. The village headman is Lv 4; the bandit chief is Lv 22. Old Qiao, who mends the bridge and settles every quarrel, is Lv 1. He has been Lv 1 for seventy-three years.
events.arc: The Old Man at Level One

choices.text: Ask Old Qiao how he lived

effects.log: "Badly at first," he says, "and then better." He hands you the other end of a plank.

choices.text: Pity him

effects.log: He notices, and laughs at you, and goes back to the bridge.

choices.text: Help him mend the bridge

effects.log: [EXP gained: 30]. You feel you have learned more than 30.

events.text: A spring flood takes the bridge. The whole village gathers, and they do not look at the headman, or at you, Lv whatever you are. They look at Old Qiao. The window flickers, confused.
events.arc: The Old Man at Level One

choices.text: Follow Old Qiao's lead

effects.log: By summer there is a new bridge. [Warning: Status window may be inaccurate].

choices.text: Take charge yourself

ok.log: It works, but every time you are stuck you end up asking Old Qiao.

fail.log: The villagers politely ignore you and do what Old Qiao says.

events.text: Old Qiao dies in his sleep at ninety. At the funeral the whole valley comes, more than came for the governor. The window shows his name one last time: [Qiao. Lv 1]. Then, after a long pause, the number changes.
events.arc: The Old Man at Level One

choices.text: Look at what it changed to

effects.log: It does not show a number. It shows a bridge.

choices.text: Close the window and carry the coffin

effects.log: You are one of eight. None of you has a level. Today none of you needs one.

events.text: [Party Bonus Available: +20% EXP]. You need two companions. The only people in town are Smith Zhao, who hates everyone, and Ma the herbalist, who talks to plants. The old silver mine has bandits in it.

choices.text: Recruit both and clear the mine

ok.log: Zhao hits things, Ma heals things, you shout directions. [Dungeon Cleared]. (60 taels)

fail.log: Zhao and Ma argue at the mine mouth for an hour and the bandits leave out of embarrassment.

choices.text: Go in alone

ok.log: No bonus, but no arguing either.

fail.log: You come out faster than you went in.

choices.text: Leave the mine to the magistrate

effects.log: The magistrate sends three men and a dog. The dog does the most.

events.text: Smith Zhao turns up at your door with a sabre he has made for you, without being asked, and leaves without saying a word. Ma the herbalist sends a pot of mint. The window shows: [Party: Still Formed].

choices.text: Invite them both for dinner

effects.log: Zhao talks to the mint. Ma hits the table. It is the best evening in months.

choices.text: Take the party on the road for a season

effects.log: Three bandit camps and one very confused tiger. [Party Achievement: Odd Company].

events.text: A rich merchant's wedding, red silk everywhere. A message burns across your sight: [The Drunken Immortal Who Laughs at Heaven] is bored. [The Drunken Immortal] will pay 25 coins if you trip in front of the bride's family.
events.arc: The Star Who Wanted a Fall

choices.text: Trip, spectacularly

effects.log: Three teacups, one roast duck and a very surprised uncle. Somewhere above, a star is crying with laughter.

choices.text: Trip, but catch every cup on the way down

ok.log: You fall, roll, and come up with nine cups in your hands. The guests applaud. [The Drunken Immortal] applauds too.

fail.log: You catch none of them. The duck is a loss.

choices.text: Refuse: it is their day

effects.log: [The Judge of the Bright Hall] nods. [The Drunken Immortal] calls you a stick in the mud.

events.text: The bride from the wedding, now a matron with three children, stops you in the street. "You," she says. "The duck. My husband and I still laugh about it every new year. It was the best part of the day."
events.arc: The Star Who Wanted a Fall

choices.text: Confess it was for a star

effects.log: She does not believe a word and laughs even harder. [The Drunken Immortal] sends 10 coins out of sheer joy.

choices.text: Pay for a new duck at last

effects.log: She takes the silver and buys everyone noodles with it. (-8 taels)

events.text: On the Willow Bridge a thief snatches a purse and a merchant falls into the river in one breath. The sky lights up: [The Judge of the Bright Hall] bids 20 for the rescue. [The Fox Behind the Nine Screens] bids 25 for the purse.

choices.text: Dive for the merchant

ok.log: You haul him onto the bank, coughing. [The Judge] is pleased.

fail.log: You both nearly drown, but a ferryman pulls you both out.

choices.text: Chase the thief

ok.log: You catch him in an alley and keep the purse. [The Fox] is very pleased. (30 taels)

fail.log: The thief knows the alleys better. The stars groan as one.

choices.text: Do both: throw the thief into the river after the merchant

effects.log: The thief holds the merchant up out of sheer fright. Even [The Lord of a Hundred Battlefields] laughs.

events.text: The merchant you pulled out of the river, Wen Guang, sends for you. He would like to pay you, but more than that, he would like to know who you were talking to as you dived. "You said: 'Twenty? Fine.'"

choices.text: Tell him about the stars

effects.log: He listens very seriously and then lights incense to the sky every night. The stars are flattered.

choices.text: Say you were counting

effects.log: He laughs and gives you forty taels and a standing table at his restaurant. (40 taels)

events.text: The purse from the Willow Bridge had a letter in it, and the letter was from a mother to her son in the army. [The Fox Behind the Nine Screens] says: keep it, it is leverage. [The Judge] says nothing, pointedly.

choices.text: Deliver the letter to the barracks

effects.log: The soldier reads it twice and puts it inside his armour. [The Judge] sends 15 coins at last.

choices.text: Keep it: the Fox is your friend

effects.log: [The Fox] purrs. The letter sits in a drawer and you think of it more than you would like.

events.text: No message for a whole season. No coins. When you finally ask the sky, a single grey line appears: [Your sponsor has turned its face away]. Apparently it did not like the last thing you did. It will not say what.

choices.text: Apologise to the sky at the shrine

effects.log: You burn incense and say sorry to the night. A small, grudging coin falls.

choices.text: Go out and do something it loves

ok.log: You guess right. A flood of messages: your sponsor was only waiting to be won back.

fail.log: You guess wrong. Another star likes it. Your sponsor sulks harder.

choices.text: Let it sulk

effects.log: You live your own life for a season. It is very quiet up there.

events.text: A message, very small, at midnight: [Your sponsor wonders if you are angry with it]. Then, before you can answer: [Your sponsor did not mean anything by it]. Then: [Your sponsor is not sulking].

choices.text: Tell it you missed it

effects.log: The sky over your house is clear for a week, and the coins come back double for a month.

choices.text: Tell it to keep its own taste and you yours

effects.log: A long pause. Then: [Your sponsor respects that]. It sounds surprised.

events.text: The shrine priest where you burned incense to the sky, a round little man called Brother Dou, says the shrine has never had such luck: three new bells given in a year. He wonders, with a wink, what you said to the stars.

choices.text: Help him hang the bells

effects.log: The bells ring in the wind every night. Something above seems to enjoy them.

choices.text: Give a fourth bell

effects.log: Four bells. [Your sponsor] says it can hear them. (-20 taels)

events.text: A friendly bout at the Spring Lantern fair, against the boatman Hu Da. [The Lord of a Hundred Battlefields] offers 40 coins if Hu Da does not walk out of the ring. [The Drunken Immortal] offers 20 for a good show.
events.arc: The Stars Want Blood, You Give Them a Show

choices.text: Give them a good show

ok.log: Somersaults, a paper umbrella from the crowd, a dunk in the fish pond. Hu Da laughs until he falls over. Nobody is hurt.

fail.log: You fall in the fish pond first. It still counts as a show.

choices.text: Win quickly and cleanly

ok.log: Three moves and a bow. [The Lord of a Hundred Battlefields] grumbles at your restraint.

fail.log: Hu Da is stronger than he looks. You both eat after.

choices.text: Tell the war star no out loud

effects.log: [The Monkey Who Struck the Heavens] likes that very much. The crowd thinks you are odd.

events.text: Hu Da the boatman has told the story of the fish pond bout so many times that the fair has made it a custom: every spring, a mock duel, and the loser goes in the pond. They want you to open it.
events.arc: The Stars Want Blood, You Give Them a Show

choices.text: Open it and go in the pond yourself

effects.log: [The Drunken Immortal] declares it the best custom on earth. You are wet but famous.

choices.text: Open it and push Hu Da in

effects.log: Hu Da goes in with a roar and comes out with a carp.

events.text: [The Moon Who Ties Red Threads] has chosen for you: the ferry captain, Lady Ou, steady hands, scar on her chin. Coins will rain, it promises, at the first sign of romance. Lady Ou, for her part, only wants your fare.
events.arc: The Red Thread That Was Not There

choices.text: Pay the fare and leave it there

effects.log: She nods. [The Moon] sends a disappointed sigh across the whole sky. (-1 taels)

choices.text: Make conversation

ok.log: She tells you about the river for an hour. She is not interested in you; she is interested in the river.

fail.log: She asks if you would like to swim the rest of the way.

choices.text: Tell the star to mind its own heavens

effects.log: [The Monkey Who Struck the Heavens] cheers. [The Moon] sulks at the Monkey.

events.text: You have crossed the river with Lady Ou fifty times now, and become friends of the plainest kind. [The Moon Who Ties Red Threads] has given up on you. Today Lady Ou asks if you know a good matchmaker, for her brother.
events.arc: The Red Thread That Was Not There

choices.text: Ask the Moon for help, properly this time

effects.log: The brother meets a tailor at the ferry. The Moon is very pleased with itself, and takes all the credit.

choices.text: Introduce the brother to someone yourself

effects.log: It goes very well. [The Moon] pretends it was its idea and pays you anyway.

events.text: Tax Collector Peng has been taking a third more than the law allows from the river villages for years. [The Fox Behind the Nine Screens] has a plan, and offers 25 coins for it: forge a letter from the governor.

choices.text: Forge the letter

ok.log: The governor's seal is perfect. Peng reads it, goes grey and returns the silver.

fail.log: The ink is a shade too blue. A year in the county cell.

choices.text: Do it honestly: take the books to the prefect

effects.log: [The Judge of the Bright Hall] outbids the Fox. Peng is sent to a fishing village to count fish.

choices.text: Refuse both stars

effects.log: The stars sulk. The villages keep paying.

events.text: Peng's replacement, a sharp young official, is asking questions about a letter that the governor never wrote. [The Fox Behind the Nine Screens] is delighted: [A second act!]

choices.text: Plant a trail that leads nowhere

ok.log: Three weeks later the official is sure the letter was written by a ghost. [The Fox] sends a gift.

fail.log: The trail leads to you, more or less. You leave the county in a hurry.

choices.text: Tell her the truth

effects.log: She listens, writes for a long time, and then burns the page. "Peng was a thief," she says. "You were only a forger."

events.text: The notebook, in your own cramped hand: "Do not cross the Huai bridge at Stone Mill in spring. It falls. Go round." Today you are at Stone Mill, it is spring, and going round costs two days and the last of your silver.

choices.text: Go round

effects.log: Two days of mud and an inn with fleas. (-15 taels)

choices.text: Cross, carefully

ok.log: The bridge holds. It does not even creak.

fail.log: A plank gives under one foot, nothing more. The bridge stands.

choices.text: Warn the travellers at the bridge

effects.log: Nobody believes you. Two carters go round anyway, to be safe.

events.text: In a teahouse at Stone Mill an old mason, Master Kong, tells the story: last autumn a stranger paid him to reinforce the old bridge with iron pins, "because it would fall in spring". He shows you the stranger's note, in your hand.

choices.text: Ask him who the stranger was

effects.log: He describes you, older, tired, with a limp you do not have. Yet.

choices.text: Read the note again

effects.log: It says: "If you read this, it worked. The book is right even when it is wrong."

choices.text: Pay him for his work

effects.log: He did it for nothing, he says. He takes the silver anyway. (-20 taels)

events.text: Years pass. The notebook's spring tip about the Huai bridge has quietly changed. In your hand, newer ink: "The bridge holds. Thank Kong." Master Kong is very old now and has asked to see you.

choices.text: Go and thank him

effects.log: He grins with three teeth. "I did not do it for you," he says. "I did it for the bridge."

choices.text: Pay for his grandson to learn the trade

effects.log: The grandson pins his first bridge at sixteen. (-30 taels)

events.text: Between the tips for your thirties and your forties a page is gone, torn out close to the binding. On the next page, in your hand: "Do not look for it." The torn edge is old and brown, as if it was torn a long time ago.

choices.text: Look for it

effects.log: Of course you look for it.

choices.text: Do as you say

effects.log: You close the notebook. It takes a long time to stop thinking about it.

choices.text: Write a question on the next page

effects.log: You write: "Why?" Nothing answers, but the ink never dries.

events.text: A pawnshop in the provincial capital is selling a box of old letters. In it, folded small, a page in your own hand, brown at the edge. The pawnbroker wants a ridiculous forty taels for the box.

choices.text: Buy the box

effects.log: Forty taels for a page you wrote. (-40 taels)

choices.text: Read the page in the shop and put it back

ok.log: You read it in one breath while the pawnbroker counts coins.

fail.log: He catches you and throws you out. The page stays in the box.

choices.text: Leave it: you were told

effects.log: You walk out. Behind you, the box sells to someone else.

events.text: The torn page says only one thing, in your hand, pressed hard: "You will lose someone you could not have saved. It is not your fault. I tore this out so you would not spend ten years being afraid of it."

choices.text: Burn the page

effects.log: It burns slowly. You feel lighter than you have in years.

choices.text: Put it back in the notebook

effects.log: You paste it in carefully. The next you will need it.

events.text: The notebook: "Lu Wenqing. Smiles with one side of the face. Do not let him into the house." Today a tea merchant with a lopsided smile comes to your door. His card says Lu Wenqing. He is selling very good tea, cheap.
events.arc: The One the Notebook Warns About

choices.text: Shut the door

effects.log: He bows and goes. His tea smells wonderful through the door.

choices.text: Let him in and watch him closely

ok.log: He looks once too long at your strongbox. You note it and say nothing.

fail.log: You watch the wrong hand. Thirty taels go missing. (-30 taels)

choices.text: Buy tea at the gate

effects.log: The tea is very good. You still do not let him in. (-3 taels)

events.text: Lu Wenqing turns up again, this time in the magistrate's yard: arrested for robbing four houses in the district. He sees you in the crowd and gives you his half-smile. "You knew," he says. "How did you know?"
events.arc: The One the Notebook Warns About

choices.text: Testify against him

effects.log: He is sent to the salt works. The notebook's line about him goes faint.

choices.text: Tell him: a friend warned me

effects.log: He laughs. "Then you have better friends than I do."

events.text: The notebook's line about Lu Wenqing has changed. It now reads: "Lu Wenqing. He came back. He brought tea. Let him in this time." There is a knock at the door. It is very gentle.
events.arc: The One the Notebook Warns About

choices.text: Let him in

effects.log: He is greyer, quieter, and he only wants to say he works an honest stall now. The tea is still very good.

choices.text: Speak through the door

effects.log: He leaves the tea on the step and a note: "Thank you for not letting me in."

events.text: Among disasters and betrayals, in the margin, a recipe: "Pork and chive dumplings, the way the Liu stall did them. You will want this at forty. Trust me." It is quite detailed. There is a drawing of the fold.

choices.text: Make them now

ok.log: They are wonderful, and you have no idea why you will want them at forty.

fail.log: They fall apart. The drawing of the fold is harder than it looks.

choices.text: Find the Liu stall

effects.log: Old Liu sells them in the east market. They are exactly as described. (-2 taels)

choices.text: Ignore it: there are disasters to plan for

effects.log: You read the flood tip again. The margin waits.

events.text: Old Liu's dumpling stall is closing: no one to take it over. Old Liu shrugs. "Recipes die," he says. "Like people." The notebook's margin note is very specific about the fold.

choices.text: Learn the stall from Old Liu

effects.log: A month in his kitchen. He says your fold is wrong. Then he says it is right.

choices.text: Pay his niece to keep it open

effects.log: The niece is good. The dumplings live on. (-50 taels)

events.text: At forty you have a very bad winter: a fever, a loss, an empty house. You remember, from nowhere, the margin note, and stand in the kitchen with flour on your hands, folding the way the drawing shows.

choices.text: Make enough for the whole street

effects.log: The neighbours come out into the snow. You were right. You wanted this at forty.

choices.text: Make enough for one and eat them slowly

effects.log: The you who wrote it knew this winter. They left you dumplings for it.

events.text: Underlined twice: "The scholar in grey at the Ninefold Library also remembers. Be kind to him; he did not have a notebook." At the library a scholar in grey looks up from his scroll as you enter and goes very still.

choices.text: Sit across from him and wait

effects.log: After an hour he says, "You too?" and starts to cry.

choices.text: Leave him be

effects.log: He watches you leave. The next day he is gone from the library.

choices.text: Ask him what he remembers

ok.log: Everything, he says. Every year of it. Without anything written down.

fail.log: He says he has no idea what you mean, and leaves by the side door.

events.text: Scholar Ji, the man in grey, has been carrying a whole life in his head with no book to keep it in. He has been afraid to change anything. He asks to read your notebook, just once.

choices.text: Let him read it

effects.log: He reads all night, laughing at the dumpling page. In the morning he buys his own notebook.

choices.text: Read him only one page

effects.log: You pick a page with nothing frightening on it. He is grateful all the same.

events.text: A package from Scholar Ji: his own notebook, finished, in his small careful hand, with a letter. "For whoever comes after me," it says, "and since nobody comes after me, for you."

choices.text: Read it

effects.log: A whole other life, lived twice. In it, you are a kind stranger at a library.

choices.text: Place it in the Ninefold Library, among the histories

effects.log: It is shelved as fiction. Scholar Ji would have laughed.

events.text: The dyke breaks at night. From the roof you see two boats overturned in the brown water: one with the ferryman's three children, one with the old magistrate and his clerk. You have one rope. Ding. [Simulation available].

choices.text: Run the simulation

effects.log: Two glimpses flash past: in one, the children cling to a roof beam and live; in the other, nobody reaches the magistrate in time.

choices.text: Throw the rope to the children

ok.log: Three small hands on the rope. You pull until your arms shake.

fail.log: The rope slips once; a neighbour catches the smallest one. All three live.

choices.text: Throw the rope to the magistrate

ok.log: The old magistrate comes up the rope wheezing, his clerk on his back.

fail.log: The clerk makes it; the magistrate clings to a tree until dawn.

events.text: The glimpse shows the children holding a roof beam, alive at dawn. The magistrate in the water, alone. You have the rope still in your hands, and the vision fading. A glimpse is a likely path, not a promise.

choices.text: Trust it: rope to the magistrate

effects.log: You pull him out. At dawn the children are on the roof beam, exactly as you saw, cold and alive.

choices.text: Do not trust it: rope to the children

effects.log: The children are safe. The magistrate is found at noon, holding a tree.

events.text: Years after the flood, a letter comes from the ferryman's eldest, now a dyke engineer, and one from the old magistrate's clerk, now a magistrate himself. Both say thank you. Both want you at the new dyke's opening.

choices.text: Go to the opening

effects.log: You stand between them on the new dyke. The river is low and brown and harmless.

choices.text: Send a gift and stay home

effects.log: You send a carved boat. They hang it over the dyke gate. (-10 taels)

events.text: The ferryman's three children, grown, come to your door with a basket of river fish, every year on the night of the flood. They never say why. They do not need to. This year the youngest has brought her own child.

choices.text: Cook the fish together

effects.log: Four generations of a family that should not exist, eating fish at your table.

choices.text: Ask what became of the magistrate

effects.log: He lived, it turns out, holding a tree, and retired cursing the river every day.

events.text: You run the simulation on a small thing, whether to take the mountain road home or the river road, and see yourself lying very still beside the river. Ding. [Glimpse complete. Probability: likely]. Then nothing.

choices.text: Take the mountain road

effects.log: Three days of climbing. Nothing happens, which is the point.

choices.text: Take the river road anyway

ok.log: At the place you saw, a drunk boatman is lying by the river, very still, asleep. He looks like you from a distance.

fail.log: A rockfall on the river road misses you by an arm. You lie very still beside the river for an hour, shaking.

choices.text: Run it again

effects.log: The second glimpse shows the same river and you, older, fishing. The Simulator says nothing about the difference.

events.text: You keep thinking of the glimpse. Ding. [Note: A glimpse is drawn from the odds on the day it is run. The odds of a day are not the odds of a life]. It is the most the Simulator has ever said to you.

choices.text: Thank it

effects.log: [One glimpse returned]. You did not know it could do that.

choices.text: Go fishing on the river road

effects.log: You catch nothing all day by the river. You have never been so happy to be alive.

events.text: Your old friend Tang Shu wants you to go in with him on a silk shop in the capital. The Simulator is ready: [Run simulation? Uses left this decade: shown]. Tang Shu is looking at you. He will see it if you look away.
events.arc: The Choice You Did Not Simulate

choices.text: Say yes without looking

effects.log: You shake his hand. The Simulator closes with a small, offended click. (-50 taels)

choices.text: Run it

effects.log: The glimpse is dull and good: a shop, a counter, two friends arguing about the price of dye.

choices.text: Say no

effects.log: Tang Shu shrugs and goes alone. You hear later the shop does fine.

events.text: The silk shop has a bad first year, then a good second, then a flood in the warehouse that ruins half the stock. Through it all Tang Shu has never asked whether you looked. Tonight, drunk on cheap wine, he does.
events.arc: The Choice You Did Not Simulate

choices.text: Tell him the truth: you did not look

effects.log: He cries a little and pays you back your share with interest. (80 taels)

choices.text: Tell him you saw it all go well

effects.log: It is not quite a lie. He believes you, and works harder.

events.text: The silk shop thrives, as the glimpse said. Tang Shu tells everyone you have a nose for business. You never tell him about the glimpse, and it sits between you, a very small stone in a very comfortable shoe.
events.arc: The Choice You Did Not Simulate

choices.text: Tell him at last

effects.log: He is quiet for a day. Then he asks you to look at his daughter's match for him.

choices.text: Keep it to yourself

effects.log: Your share of the profit is sixty taels this year. The stone stays in the shoe. (60 taels)

events.text: Ding. [Notice: The host has run the simulation on breakfast]. Pork bun or red bean bun. The Simulator shows both: in one you are full, in the other you are full. It adds: [Glimpses are meant for big choices].

choices.text: Run it again on the tea

effects.log: [Warning: Frivolous Use]. In both glimpses you spill it.

choices.text: Eat both buns

effects.log: The Simulator sighs, if a Simulator can sigh. (-1 taels)

choices.text: Apologise to the Simulator

effects.log: [Apology logged]. It seems mollified.

events.text: A big choice at last: a sect elder offers to take you as a personal disciple, if you leave tonight. The Simulator pipes up before you even ask: [Now THIS is what I am for].

choices.text: Run it, gladly

effects.log: The glimpse is long and full of hard training. You leave tonight. [Satisfaction: high].

choices.text: Decide on your own, to tease it

effects.log: You choose. The Simulator does not speak to you for a month.

events.text: You are small, and the persimmon tree in the temple yard is very tall, and the best fruit is at the top. A cold, clear voice speaks for the first time: [Life Simulator: first use free]. You see yourself falling.

choices.text: Climb anyway, more carefully

ok.log: You choose your branches as if you have done it before. The persimmon is perfect.

fail.log: You fall from the third branch, as you saw, and land in the monk's cabbages. Not as far as you saw.

choices.text: Wait for the monk with the long pole

effects.log: He knocks down three persimmons and gives you one. You learn that ladders exist.

choices.text: Run home terrified of the voice

effects.log: You do not sleep for two nights. The voice says nothing more, as if it is sorry.

events.text: The Simulator still speaks to you sometimes, in its cold clear voice. Today, when an older boy dares you to jump off the mill roof, it says only: [Glimpse: you will be fine, and he will not].

choices.text: Talk him out of jumping

ok.log: He climbs down, sulking. A week later the mill roof falls in by itself.

fail.log: He jumps anyway and breaks a wrist. You run for the bonesetter.

choices.text: Tell the miller

effects.log: The miller chases you both off with a broom. Nobody jumps.

events.text: Ding. [Villain Quest: Assemble Your Henchmen]. A notice at the crossroads, and by noon three candidates are in your hall: Big Tiger Ma, who has a very large axe; Scholar Pu, who has an abacus; and the Hu twins, who have each other.

choices.text: Take Big Tiger Ma

effects.log: He bows so low he knocks over a candle. [VP +10: Intimidating Staff].

choices.text: Take Scholar Pu

effects.log: He has already found three errors in your accounts. [VP +10: Competent Staff].

choices.text: Take the Hu twins

effects.log: Neither of them knows which one you chose. [VP +10: Confusing Staff].

choices.text: Ask each for their evil laugh

effects.log: Ma roars, Pu clears his throat, the twins laugh in harmony. You take all of them on trial.

events.text: First job: frighten the salt merchant guild into selling you their docks. [Villain Quest: Use Your Henchmen]. Your new henchman is very keen, and has been sharpening something since dawn.

choices.text: Send Big Tiger Ma

effects.log: Ma walks into the guild hall and sits down. That is all he does. They sell.

choices.text: Send Scholar Pu

effects.log: Pu finds the guild has not paid its river tax in ten years. They sell, cheaply. (120 taels)

choices.text: Send the Hu twins

effects.log: The guildmaster sees one twin leave and the other arrive in the same breath and thinks you have ghosts. He sells.

choices.text: Go yourself

effects.log: You do it yourself. Your henchman sulks in the hall.

events.text: Ding. [Henchman Review Due]. The System wants a mark from one to five. Your henchman stands in front of you, twisting a hat, having heard about the review from the cook, who hears everything.

choices.text: Five, and a raise

effects.log: Loyalty locked in. [The System notes: soft]. (-20 taels)

choices.text: Three: room to grow

effects.log: [The System approves of your management style].

choices.text: Let them leave with a good word

effects.log: They go home to their village and open a noodle stall. [The System is disappointed in you].

events.text: Ding. [Evaluation: Villainous Laugh]. [Grade: D-]. [Note: the host's laugh resembles a hen startled by a pot]. The System suggests lessons. It has, it says, found you a teacher: a retired opera villain called Ah Gong.

choices.text: Take lessons from Ah Gong

effects.log: Ah Gong listens to you laugh and covers his ears. (-15 taels)

choices.text: Practise alone on the mountain

ok.log: [Grade: C]. A goatherd runs away. Progress.

fail.log: The echo laughs back better than you do.

choices.text: Refuse: real villains do not laugh

effects.log: [Grade: Incomplete. Interesting choice].

events.text: Ah Gong, eighty years old and missing three teeth, has taught you the three laughs of the opera villain: the low chuckle, the rising cackle, and the silence before. "The silence is the worst," he says, "and the best."

choices.text: Laugh for the System

ok.log: [Grade: A]. The whole inn falls silent. Ah Gong weeps with pride.

fail.log: [Grade: B-]. Ah Gong says the silence was good, the cackle cracked.

choices.text: Do the silence only

effects.log: You look at a drunk who is bothering the singer and say nothing. He leaves. [Grade: S].

events.text: [Villain Quest: Steal a Fortuitous Encounter]. A young wanderer, not Heaven's chosen but trying very hard, is about to fall off a cliff and land, by pure chance, in a cave with a grandmaster's manual. The System wants it first.

choices.text: Climb down and take the manual

ok.log: You are out of the cave before the wanderer stops falling. They land on a pile of moss and nothing else.

fail.log: You fall too. The wanderer lands on you. The manual is soaked.

choices.text: Catch the wanderer before they fall

effects.log: They thank you and walk away, never knowing what they missed.

choices.text: Watch to see what happens

effects.log: The wanderer lands in the cave, reads the manual upside down and leaves without learning a thing.

events.text: The wanderer from the cliff has become a passable swordsman, by work and no miracles. They come to you, of all people, for advice. They do not know. The System has suggestions: all unkind.

choices.text: Give them honest advice

effects.log: They improve. [The System makes a note in red].

choices.text: Teach them a technique with a flaw

effects.log: [VP +15]. One day someone will see the flaw. It may not be you.

choices.text: Tell them about the cave

effects.log: They laugh until they cry. "I hit every branch," they say. "Every one."

events.text: The grandmaster's manual from the cave turns out to have a last page you had not read, a note to the finder: "May this go to someone who fell by accident." The System says it is irrelevant.

choices.text: Give the manual to the wanderer

effects.log: They read it the right way up this time.

choices.text: Keep it: you fell on purpose

effects.log: [VP +10]. The System is pleased. You are less pleased than you expected.

events.text: Ding. [Lair Rating: Poor]. [Current lair: a rented room above a tofu shop]. The System wants a cave, a waterfall, or at minimum a ruined temple. The tofu seller, Widow Dong, has just brought up your morning tofu.

choices.text: Find a ruined temple

effects.log: It is draughty, haunted by bats and very impressive. (-40 taels)

choices.text: Make the tofu room more sinister

effects.log: Black curtains, one candle. Widow Dong thinks you are ill and brings soup.

choices.text: Stay: the tofu is good

effects.log: [Lair Rating: Still Poor]. The tofu is very good.

events.text: The ruined temple has bats, a leaking roof and a family of foxes, and the villagers below have started leaving offerings at the gate because they think you are a mountain spirit. Ding. [Fear Rating: Rising].

choices.text: Encourage it: wear a mask

effects.log: The offerings double. So do the rumours.

choices.text: Go down and tell them the truth

effects.log: They are disappointed. The headman asks if you can at least scare the tax collector.

events.text: Widow Dong has found out what you are. She leans on the doorframe with a tray of tofu. "A villain," she says. "Upstairs. Well, you pay on time, which is more than the scholar did."

choices.text: Ask her to keep it quiet

effects.log: She says she has no idea what you mean, loudly, to the whole street.
